summary.name: CalDAV
summary.one_liner: CalDAV (Calendaring Extensions to WebDAV) is an Internet standard, defined in RFC 4791, for accessing, managing, and sharing calendar data and scheduling meetings across servers.
use_cases: Sync a calendar across multiple devices
Share calendars with other users or organizations
summary.what_it_does: CalDAV is an IETF standard that extends WebDAV so clients can access and manage calendar data and schedule meetings with users on the same or remote servers. It stores events, tasks, free-busy information, and notes in collections and resources, using the iCalendar format. The specification requires servers to support WebDAV Access Control (RFC 3744) so permissions can be set per user and operation. Servers handle calendar-specific operations such as free-busy reports and expansion of recurring events. The page describes the protocol and its history, not a specific implementation.
notable: Open IETF standard, published as RFC 4791 in March 2007
Built on WebDAV and uses iCalendar data format
Requires WebDAV Access Control Protocol (RFC 3744) for per-user permissions
caveats: The page describes a protocol standard, not a single installable product
The article notes it needs more citations
